scope: Independent review of the reset diagnostic candidate-filter correction

verdict_a.title: Finding resolution, diagnostic usefulness, and runtime status
verdict_a.evidence: The diagnostic now derives target_count and its sampled target from candidates satisfying the same checks as settings-panel-driver.click: positive layout, computed visibility not hidden, computed display not none, and no inert ancestor. It separately reports raw_target_count and whether any raw match is in an inert tree, so hidden/inert exact-text duplicates no longer inflate the eligible count. The driver still rejects any candidate count other than one before hit-testing; the diagnostic nevertheless hit-tests targets[0] when multiple eligible candidates exist, so target_hit then describes only the first eligible candidate rather than a uniquely selected native target.

finding.detail: The original raw-versus-eligible mismatch is fixed. A residual ambiguity remains when multiple candidates pass the shared filter: the native driver stops at uniqueness failure, while the diagnostic samples the first eligible candidate.
finding.recommendation: When target_count is not exactly one, omit target-specific hit/layout/viewport/animation facts or make their first-candidate scope explicit; the guarded retry remains necessary for runtime evidence.

verdict_a.limitations: No browser/runtime execution was performed. The prior receipts still do not establish a product reset defect or behavior after Confirm.

verdict_b.title: Safety and source quality
verdict_b.evidence: The diff adds only counts and boolean facts for candidate filtering; no raw text, URL, exception, storage value, credential, or auth material is serialized. It changes only failure diagnostics. The native click sequence and post-confirm storage/sign-out acceptance assertions are unchanged.
